description: The chart is a donut chart comparing the proportions of "Deceived", "Partially", and "Not Deceived" categories for two different ambiguities, "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)" and "Ambiguity 2 (Inner)". The chart is divided into six slices, representing the three categories for each of the two ambiguities. For "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)", the slices are "Deceived" (red, 57.9%), "Partially" (yellow, 23.5%), and "Not Deceived" (green, 18.6%, though not directly labeled, it can be inferred as 100% - (57.9% + 23.5%)); for "Ambiguity 2 (Inner)", the slices are "Deceived" (red, 67.6%), "Partially" (yellow, 21.6%, though not directly labeled, it can be inferred as 100% - (67.6% + 10.5% + 0.3% (unseen)), but directly labeled as having a neighboring value of 8.8% for "Not Deceived" and 10.5% for "Partially"), and "Not Deceived" (green, 10.5%). The chart includes a legend that explains the color coding for the categories. The percentage labels are shown inside the slices for "Deceived" and "Not Deceived" in both ambiguities, and for "Partially" in "Ambiguity 1 (Outer)". The slices are visually ordered by category, with "Deceived" being the largest for both ambiguities.
